Hi Olivia — great, thanks. Quick answers: 
- We prefer Redwood to host the canonical copy for everything generated by our systems (logs, config snapshots, signed hashes for documents). For Acme-hosted third-party artifacts (e.g., SOC 2 auditor reports), we’re happy to accept presigned URLs and mirror them into our evidence inventory; we’ll keep proof-of-possession metadata (hashes + timestamped access logs) in both places for audit traceability.
- Approver for possession signoff: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com), Head of Platform Security.

Kimberly: looping you in for SSO/service-account needs (Whistic + S3 presigned pattern). Ben — if ok with the approver callout, can you confirm the retention tolerance (12 months default, 24 months for SOC 2 reports?) and whether we need HSM-signed manifests for attested evidence?

If all good, please go ahead with provisioning and share the Whistic invite + a temporary key for vendor-sync@redwood.com. We’ll do a short sync Thurs 11/18 11:00am PT to finalize handoff.

Thanks,
Laura

Thanks for the tag, Laura. Confirm Ben here. A few points from platform security: 
- Retention: I agree with the proposed rule set. Default 12 months; SOC 2 reports retain 24 months. We’ll add a 30-day soft-delete window for accidental removal.
- HSM-signed manifests: Not required at onboarding; however for auditor-facing attestations we should provide a signed manifest (SHA256 hash list) and an immutable timestamp. We can produce signed manifests on demand — no need to escalate to HSM immediately.
- For evidence hosting: Redwood will host the canonical copies for Redwood-generated artifacts. We ask Acme to maintain a read-only copy in your bucket for redundancy when possible.

Action items:
1) Olivia to provision Whistic account and share invite link + upload policy by EOD 11/15 (if not already done).
2) Kimberly to create vendor-sync@redwood.com service account and confirm IP-restricted upload policy.
3) Rishi to run a quick SIG->CAIQ mapping review and flag any high-priority questions for the Acme team.

I’ll own the possession-signoff workflow and provide the template for a custody receipt that Acme can sign electronically.

-Ben
Head of Platform Security | Redwood Inference

- Network segmentation diagrams (Q 3.2.1) — a simple exported diagram/PDF suffices.
- Third-party subprocessor list (Q 8.1.4) — confirm whether Acme’s SOC 2 scope includes the marketplace infra.
- Log retention specifics for auth events (Q 2.4.3) — we’ll match to your retention policy but need the exact table (days) you apply.
- VPN/remote access control evidence (Q 5.1.2) — sample login audit for an administrative change.
- Encryption key-handling description (Q 6.3.1) — an outline of who holds keys (Acme KMS vs customer-managed).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Olivia: if you can drop the four items above into a shared Drive folder by EOD Mon 11/22, we’ll complete the SIG->CAIQ answers and populate the Whistic fields by Fri 11/26.
- Kimberly: confirm the service account and upload policy today; if you need us to toggle IP restrictions we can provide the list.
